q: Inside `case "swish":`, what does TypeScript know about `p`?
options: `p` is `{ method: "swish"; phone: string }`, so `p.phone` is a `string`
`p` is still `Payment`, so you need `p.phone!` or a cast
Nothing: narrowing only works with `if`, not `switch`
explain: Checking the tag narrows the **whole object**. Only one shape has `method: "swish"`, so `p` is that shape and `p.phone` is a plain `string`. No cast or `!` is needed. `switch` narrows exactly like `if (p.method === "swish")` does.

q: A teammate adds `{ method: "klarna"; months: number }` to `Payment`. Which version of `show` turns that into a **compile error** until klarna is handled?
explain: In B, after the card and swish cases, `p` is the klarna shape, which isn't assignable to `never`, so the call to `assertNever` is an error. A compiles forever, because returning `""` is fine for any shape: that's the blank grey card. C compiles too, because falling off the end just returns `undefined`, which the return type allows.

q: Which statements about `never` are true? Select all that apply.
options: A function that always throws can have return type `never`
When every case of a union has been handled, the leftover type is `never`
`assertNever` can never run, so it doesn't need a body
explain: `never` is the empty type: no values at all. A function that always throws never *returns*, so `never` is its honest return type. Narrowing away every shape leaves `never`. It is **not** `undefined`, which is a real value. And `assertNever` does need a body: types are erased, so bad data from an API can still reach the `default` at runtime, and the `throw` makes that loud.

q: Why doesn't this narrow `s` to the open shape?
options: The tag is typed `string` in both shapes, so `"open"` could belong to either. It must be a literal type like `"open"`
Narrowing only works on a field called `kind` or `type`
You have to use `switch` to narrow on a tag
explain: A discriminant only works if each shape gives it a different **literal** type. With `state: string` everywhere, knowing `s.state === "open"` rules nothing out. Change the shapes to `state: "open"` and `state: "closed"` and the check narrows. The field can have any name, and `if` with `===` narrows just as well as `switch`.
